title: Pensions and Postretirement Benefits - ASC 715
learning_objectives: Distinguish defined benefit from defined contribution plans

defined_contribution.accounting: Expense = Contribution amount. Simple - no complex calculations.

defined_benefit.description: Employer promises specific benefit at retirement
defined_benefit.risk: Employer bears investment risk and longevity risk

pension_expense_components.service_cost: PV of benefits earned by employees during current year (always increases expense)
pension_expense_components.interest_cost: Interest on PBO (PBO × discount rate) (always increases expense)
pension_expense_components.expected_return_on_assets: Expected earnings on plan assets (reduces expense)
pension_expense_components.amortization_of_prior_service_cost: Cost of retroactive benefits spread over service period
pension_expense_components.amortization_of_gains_losses: If outside corridor, amortize excess (corridor = 10% × greater of PBO or FV of assets)
pension_expense_components.formula: Pension Expense = Service Cost + Interest Cost - Expected Return + Amortizations

funded_status.definition: Fair value of plan assets - Projected benefit obligation (PBO)
funded_status.recognition: Report funded status on balance sheet (ASC 715 requires)

pbo_vs_abo.PBO: Projected Benefit Obligation - includes future salary increases
pbo_vs_abo.ABO: Accumulated Benefit Obligation - current/past salaries only, no future increases
pbo_vs_abo.use: PBO used for expense and funded status. ABO used for certain disclosures.

other_comprehensive_income.actuarial_gains_losses: Changes in PBO or plan assets due to actuarial assumption changes → Initially to OCI, amortize to expense if outside corridor
other_comprehensive_income.prior_service_cost: Retroactive benefit changes → Initially to OCI, amortize to expense over service period

cpa_exam_tips: Service cost and interest cost always increase expense
Expected return on assets always decreases expense
Corridor amortization: If gain/loss > 10% of greater of PBO or FV assets, amortize excess

key_points: Defined benefit: Complex, employer bears risk. Defined contribution: Simple, employee bears risk
Pension expense = Service + Interest - Expected return + Amortizations
Funded status (FV assets - PBO) reported on balance sheet
Gains/losses and prior service cost flow through OCI
